text: The applicant was born in 1968.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant lives in Stryzhavka.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 12 September 2006 the applicant submitted a written notice to the mayor of Vinnytsia informing him that the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association intended to hold a demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, the officially registered chairman of the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association at the material time was a certain Igor Viktorovyh Chumak.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, the applicant was not the chairman of the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association at the material time.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, the applicant could not even be a member of the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association because, according to the Association's charter, membership was open only to persons under the age of twenty-eight.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, at the time of the relevant events the applicant was older than twenty-eight years of age and therefore ineligible for membership of the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 13 September 2006 the mayor's office of Vinnytsia forwarded the applicant's notice of the demonstration to the police.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 13 September 2006 the mayor's office of Vinnytsia requested that the police maintain public order during the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 September 2006 the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association started the picket as intended.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, several other local groups joined the picket action on 14 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, two small camping tents measuring 2 by 2 metres were erected by the walls of the regional authority building on a 15-metre wide street.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, the two small camping tents were erected for the purpose of storing handout materials and displaying the protesters' slogans.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 15 September 2006 the executive committee of Vinnytsia City Council instituted administrative proceedings seeking to restrict or prohibit the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 15 September 2006 the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia received the administrative claim lodged by the executive committee of Vinnytsia City Council.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Later on 15 September 2006 the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia allowed the claim of the executive committee of Vinnytsia City Council.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia decided that the case file contained sufficient evidence that the protesters had behaved inappropriately.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia found that the executive committee of Vinnytsia City Council did not and could not have known about a possible breach of public order by the participants of the event, which resulted in missing the time-limit for lodging a court action as required by paragraph 1 of Article 182 of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia reset the procedural time-limit for lodging the administrative action.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia found that the participants in the event installed small architectural edifices on the pavement.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia found that during the event the participants acted arrogantly, thus offending other citizens.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia found that the participants obstructed the passage of pedestrians along Soborna street.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia found that the participants endangered road users.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia found that the alleged breaches of public order were confirmed by complaints from individuals identified as Y.S. and V.Ch.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia noted that in the notice of the event it was stated that the event would be held indefinitely.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia noted that the number of protesters was not defined in the notice and could gradually increase.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia found that at any time during the picket of indeterminate length it could not be excluded that those taking part might repeatedly breach public order.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia noted that the picket may potentially encroach upon the rights and freedoms of other local residents.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia held to prohibit the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association and other persons taking part in the action from organising and carrying out peaceful assemblies in the streets and squares of Vinnytsia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia held to prohibit the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association and other persons taking part in the action from installing small architectural edifices in Vinnytsia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia ordered the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association and other persons taking part in the action to dismantle the small architectural edifices installed in the square in front of the regional administration building.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia allowed immediate enforcement of its court ruling of 15 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At 9 p.m. on 15 September 2006 the protesters were dispersed by the police.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 29 September 2006 the local registry office informed the applicant that V.Ch. and Y.S. were not registered as residents at the addresses indicated by them in their complaints lodged with the police.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 8 October 2006 the applicant lodged an appeal against the judgment of the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia of 15 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant signed the appeal against the judgment of 15 September 2006 as the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association's chairman.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant submitted that under Article 182 of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine, a plaintiff's action could not be examined when it had been lodged out of time.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant submitted that the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia's factual conclusions had been devoid of an evidentiary basis.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant submitted that there was no evidence that the protesters had breached the law, apart from the complaints by V.Ch. and Y.S., who had given false home addresses and thus could not be identified.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant complained that the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia had rejected his request that V.Ch. and Y.S. be located and summoned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant complained that the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia had rejected his request that police officers present at the site of the picket be summoned for questioning concerning the alleged breaches of the law by the protesters.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant complained that the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia had refused his request that relevant police reports documenting the purported breaches of the law be produced.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant complained that the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia had refused his request that an inspection of the picket site be carried out with a view to determining whether the tents erected by the activists could count as 'architectural structures' and whether there had been any obstruction of traffic or pedestrians.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his appeal, the applicant complained that the sanction imposed by the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia — a total and permanent ban on the Chumatskyy Shlyakh civic youth association organising peaceful assemblies in Vinnytsia — had been arbitrary and disproportionate.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 22 November 2006 the Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal examined the applicant's appeal against the judgment of the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia of 15 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal decided that, in view of the short notice of the intention to hold a picket and the indefinite period during which the participants planned to continue their demonstration, the administrative action lodged by the executive committee of Vinnytsia City Council could be accepted for examination.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal agreed with the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia's findings of fact.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal found that by installing the tents, the protesters had breached section 16 of the Populated Localities Development Act of Ukraine.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal found that by installing the tents, the protesters had breached section 18 of the Automobile Roads Act of Ukraine.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal found that the sanction imposed on the protesters by the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia had been disproportionate.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal noted that the Constitution of Ukraine generally allowed peaceful assemblies, which could therefore not be prohibited in a blanket manner.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal found that the Constitution of Ukraine did not envisage a form of assembly such as the 'picketing' of administrative buildings with the installation on the streets of small architectural structures.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal found that the term 'peaceful assemblies' in the operative part of the Leninskiy District Court in Vinnytsia's judgment had to be substituted with the term 'pickets'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Vinnytsia Regional Court of Appeal rejected the applicant's remaining arguments as unsubstantiated.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 1 April 2009 the Higher Administrative Court of Ukraine dismissed an appeal on points of law lodged by the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that citizens have the right to assemble peacefully without arms and to hold meetings, rallies, processions and demonstrations, upon notifying in advance the bodies of executive power or bodies of local self-government.

Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that restrictions on the exercise of the right to peaceful assembly may be established by a court in accordance with the law and only in the interests of national security and public order, with the purpose of preventing disturbances or crimes, protecting the health of the population, or protecting the rights and freedoms of other persons.

Article 8(1) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that when considering a case, a court shall be governed by the principle of the rule of law, which provides that a human being and his or her rights and freedoms shall be the highest social value and shall determine the essence and orientation of the activity of the State.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 8(2) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that a court shall apply the principle of the rule of law by taking into account the case-law of the European Court of Human Rights.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 8(3) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that the right to appeal to an administrative court for the protection of human rights and freedoms based directly on a reference to the Constitution of Ukraine shall be possible.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 8(4) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that a court may not refuse to examine and resolve an administrative case on the grounds that the legislation applicable to the dispute is incomplete, unclear, incoherent, or lacking.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 11(1) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that the consideration and resolution of cases in the administrative courts shall take place on the basis of adversarial proceedings, the evidence submitted by the parties and their ability to prove its cogency before the court.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 11(2) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that the court shall consider administrative cases exclusively following the lodging of an action in accordance with the Code and may not exceed the scope of the complaints, except where necessary for the comprehensive protection of the rights, freedoms and interests of the parties or third persons.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 11(3) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that each person who seeks judicial protection may dispose of his or her claim at his or her discretion, except in the circumstances determined in the Code.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 11(4) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that the court shall use the measures provided for in law which are necessary for the establishment of all the circumstances of the case, including by determining and ordering the production of evidence on its own initiative.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 11(5) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that the court shall, on its own initiative, invite the parties to the proceedings to submit evidence or order the production of evidence which, in its view, is lacking.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 182(1) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that immediately upon receipt of a notification concerning the organisation of meetings, rallies, processions, demonstrations, etc., the executive authorities and bodies of local self-government shall have the right to apply to the District Administrative Court of the respective locality with an action seeking to prohibit these events or otherwise restrict the right to freedom of peaceful assembly.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 182(2) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that an action received on the date on which the aforementioned events take place or thereafter shall be left without examination.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 182(5) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that the court shall allow the plaintiff's claims in the interests of national security and public order where it establishes that carrying out the meetings, rallies, processions, demonstrations or other assemblies may create an imminent risk of disturbances or crimes, or endanger the health of the population or the rights and freedoms of other people, and that in its ruling the court shall indicate the manner in which the exercise of the right to peaceful assembly is to be restricted.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Article 182(6) of the Code of Administrative Justice of Ukraine (as worded at the material time) provides that the ruling of the court in respect of cases concerning restriction of the exercise of the right to peaceful assembly shall be enforced immediately.
section_path: B. Code of Administrative Justice of 6 July 2005

text: Section 16(5) of the Populated Localities Development Act of Ukraine (Law no. 2807-IV of 6 September 2005) proscribed the installation in public areas of objects for external advertisement, commercial stalls, pavilions, kiosks, and so on without authorisation.
section_path: C. Other relevant provisions of domestic law and relevant case-law

text: Section 18 of the Automobile Roads Act of Ukraine (Law no. 2862-IV of 8 September 2005) proscribed the placement of any objects, constructions, erections or their parts within the boundaries of the so-called 'red lines of the street', delimiting the width of the street.
